FOREWORD ThIs Indian Standard ( Fourth R.evision ) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Crop Protection Equipment Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Diyision Council. This standard' was first published in 1966 and subsequently revised in 1972, 1974 and 1982. The standard has been revised again to incorporate certain improvements found necessary in the Ii.ht of the modilcations sUlgested by the testios authorities and manufacturers. This revision incorporates amon, others the following: a) Amendment NJ.J. 1 to 3 issued to earlier version of the standard, b) Bditorial changes including updating of referredstandards, c) Material of construction are modified and requirement of chemical composition of brass casting components as per relevant Indian Standard is to ensure conformity, d) Provision for use of adjustable hydraulic spray nozzle, e) .Order of testing, f) Provision for supplyiq cut-off device as per purchaser's requirements, and g) Test for piston made of synthetic rubber. This standard was earlier published in two parts. With the withdrawal of IS 3906 (Part 2 ) : 1979 'Diaphragm type band-operated knapsack sprayer', this revision has been published as single standard without any part. The figures given in the standard are meant only for illustration of the components. These should not be considered as suggestive of any standard design. In preparation of this revision, considerable assistance has been derived from the pest control equipment industry and the testios authorities. For the guidance of the purchaser, Annex A has been complied. Besides quoting the number of this standard. the details desired in the Annex may also be stated. ' For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numerical values ( reviled )'. The number of significant places retained in the rounded ott value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

HAND-OPERATEDKRAPSACKSPRAYE-R, PISTON TYPE-SPECIFICATION
( Fourth Revision )
1 SCOPE 1.1 This standard prescribes material, performance, constructional and other requirements of hand-operated knapsack sprayer, piston type, used for spraying pesticides.

3.1 Agitator
A device for keeping the pesticidal material stirred in the tank. 3.2 Cycle

1.1.1 The sprayers of this type are normally used with an average working pressure of 300 kPa( 100 kPa=I�0197 kgf/em' = 1 bar).

One up and one down stroke.

3.3 Filling Hole
A hole provided for fining liquid in the tank.

2

6.11 Dell.ery Hose
A delivery hose of suitable diameter and preferably one metre in length shall be provided as agreed to between the purchaser and the supplier. Spare parts shall meet the requirements given in 7.'1. of IS 3652 : \995.

11 METHODS OF TESTS 11.1 The requirements of this specification shall be tested in accordance with the relevant clauses of IS 101'"34 : 1994. 11.1 Test for various requirements liven in the order below shall be followed by the testing authorities: . a) Dimensional and . visual check see 6.1.1, 6.1, 6.3, 6.4, 6.4.2, 6.8, 6.9.1, 6.10, 6.1%, 6.11.1, 6.13, 6.14, 6.15, 7 and 9.1; b) Mass - se� 6.16; c) Tank capacity - see 6.1 and 6.1.1;

� WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 8.1 The components of the sprayer shall have a smooth finish and shall be free from pits, burrs, sharp edges and other defects that may be detrimental to their use.
8.1 The exposed mild steel parts shall have a protective coating to prevent surface deterioration. The steel used for the hose ferrule/clip shall be plated with cadmium, zinc or nickel. chrome. Exposed brass parts may be given a suitable protective finish with clear transparent lacquer.
